audience.programmeDescription: VU Business Administration studies organisations through strategy, marketing, accounting, finance, people, law, logistics and information technology. The selected Strategy and Organisation route combines these foundations with research methods, a specialisation and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three substantive related programmes: broad business strategy and decisions; digital business and new ventures; and people, leadership and organisational change. Their business courses are supported by different analytical tools. Computational courses teach general methods rather than guaranteed business applications. Supply-chain depth, the additional advanced-accounting unit and the dedicated VU specialisation thesis remain important differences.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 60 EC in year one, 48 EC of required second-year study and two 6 EC restricted choices, then 30 EC of open academic choice, 6 EC ethics, 12 EC specialisation courses and a 12 EC individual thesis. Accounting II and Entrepreneurship are selected choices rather than requirements for every student. Noncredit research participation gates the integration-course credits. The entry language assessment and any required remediation are part of Academic Skills; personal and professional development also carries no extra credits. The usual first-year study-advice threshold is 48 EC. Minor entry, level, overlap and approval rules apply. Thesis entry requires completion of years one and two, with strict methods requirements and separate course/supervisor registration.

componentNotes.y2-07: Selected 6 EC restricted choice in period four; other permitted choices are Society and Business, Supply Chain Management II, and Technology and Innovation Management.
componentNotes.y2-09: Selected 6 EC restricted choice in period five; the alternatives are Financial Management II and Marketing II.
componentNotes.y3-01: 30 EC of open academic choice or exchange. Minor entry normally requires 90 EC; the package allows at most 6 EC introductory and at least 12 EC advanced courses, with applicable overlap and approval rules.
componentNotes.y3-05: 12 EC individual research in the selected specialisation, including a video presentation. At least four supervision meetings and four progress submissions are expected. UCR optional independent research is separate and does not establish equivalence.

notes.text: These UCR programmes provide substantive related business study, with different emphases on strategy, digital ventures or people and organisational change. They do not reproduce VU’s supply-chain sequence, advanced accounting choice or dedicated specialisation thesis. Optional independent research is separate, requires approval and is outside the displayed 24-course, 180-EC schedules; it does not replace the VU thesis. A curriculum comparison does not establish degree equivalence, professional qualification or automatic master’s admission.

It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

selectedModalDescriptions.text: Accounting & Corporate Finance introduces financial and management accounting, financial-statement preparation and analysis, costing, pricing, budgeting and organisational control. Students assess investment decisions using accounting measures, discounted cash flow, net present value, internal rate of return and cost of capital. A case study examines the misuse of an accounting principle and its effects on financial statements.

Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.

selectedModalDescriptions.text: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

selectedModalDescriptions.text: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.

Marketing & Consumer Engagement examines consumer psychology, marketing strategy, responsible brand development and customer engagement. Students analyse a company strategy, design a brand and investigate a consumer phenomenon using academic literature and primary and secondary evidence. Digital marketing and customer-journey mapping connect analysis with practical recommendations.

Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.

selectedModalDescriptions.text: Personal Leadership provides a comprehensive introduction to leadership theory and practice, designed to help students discover their unique leadership style through self-awareness and practical skill-building. Through interactive workshops, reflective exercises, and real-world applications, students engage deeply with core leadership principles and develop the tools needed to lead confidently in any setting.

This course blends theory with practice from both fiction and the real world, helping you develop essential leadership skills. Learn how to inspire teams, sharpen your communication, take ethical decisions, and lead with confidence.

Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership in diverse contexts, with particular attention to minority experiences. Students design and pilot a quantitative survey, collect data ethically, and use SPSS or RStudio for descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression. They interpret the findings and develop evidence-based leadership recommendations.
